findings.issue: 'lancheira' in Brazilian Portuguese denotes the container (lunch box/bag, cf. 弁当箱), not the packed meal itself. お弁当 refers to the boxed meal; listing 'lancheira' teaches the wrong referent.

'tão' (degree adverb, 'so') does not correspond to any EN gloss of this sense ('this kind of, such, like this'); degree use maps to こんなに, and as a standalone gloss for the pre-noun adjectival こんな it is misleading.

In pt-BR, 'estufa' primarily means greenhouse or a food-warming cabinet, not a room heater; pairing it with 'stove (heating)' can teach a misleading association. 'aquecedor' alone (or 'aquecedor a querosene/gás') is the natural pt-BR rendering of ストーブ.
In pt-BR the physical trophy is 'taça'; 'copa' names the tournament (Copa do Mundo), not the trophy object, so the parenthetical '(troféu)' is attached to the wrong word.
Romaji does not match the kana: in this file's wapuro convention 'tei' renders てい, not ティ. パーティー should be 'pa-thi-' (or Hepburn 'pātī'), not 'pa-tei-'. This is a kana mismatch, not a style variant.

First pt gloss 'sem graça (comida)' means bland/flavorless (ajinai/usui aji) rather than bad-tasting; mazui asserts the food tastes bad. Listed first, it skews the learner toward the wrong shade; the other glosses ('ruim de sabor', 'intragável') carry the correct sense.
Gloss 'que manda bem' is colloquial Brazilian slang, but the entry has register null and jouzu is register-neutral; a slang gloss in a neutral entry mixes registers without any marking.
findings.current: bom em, habilidoso, que manda bem

findings.issue: Two glosses are joined into a single array element with a comma ('umbrella, parasol'), unlike every other entry in the batch which uses one gloss per element. Data-format inconsistency; meanings themselves are correct.

それ (near the listener) maps to isso/esse in the ko-so-a system; 'aquilo' is the distal demonstrative corresponding to あれ. Including it blurs the それ/あれ distinction the course must teach and conflicts with the EN gloss '(near the listener)'.
'a frente' as a rendering of 'in front' lacks the crase ('à frente'); as written it just means 'the front', duplicating 'frente'. Natural BR options are 'à frente' or 'na frente'.
'ano após o próximo' is an unidiomatic calque of 'the year after next'; correct meaning but clearly awkward Brazilian Portuguese. The first gloss 'daqui a dois anos' is fine.
findings.current: daqui a dois anos, ano após o próximo
findings.suggested: daqui a dois anos, o ano depois do próximo
findings.fix: daqui a dois anos, o ano depois do próximo

findings.issue: Sense 'middle-aged man' does not belong to the lexeme 叔父/おじ (JMdict 1607070 = uncle only). It belongs to a different lexeme, 小父/おじさん. Attaching it here teaches that the kanji form 叔父 can mean 'middle-aged man', which is false. The pt glosses 'senhor / tio (homem de meia-idade)' inherit the same error.
findings.suggested: (delete this sense — it belongs to おじさん/小父, not to 叔父)
findings.fix: (delete this sense — it belongs to おじさん/小父, not to 叔父)

findings.issue: In Brazilian Portuguese 'moção' means a formal/parliamentary motion (moção de repúdio), not physical movement; as a gloss for 動 'motion; movement' it is a misleading near-false-friend. 'movimento' alone is sufficient.
呼ぶ is missing the core sense 'to invite' (e.g. 友達を呼ぶ = to invite friends over). This is a must-know, high-frequency meaning at N5/N4, not a rare/archaic sense; 'to summon' does not cover it.
findings.current: to call; to summon; to call out to | to name; to call (something) by a name

findings.issue: Sense pos is 'adv' but the glosses ('awful', 'tough', 'a big deal') are adjectival — they belong to the adj-na senses of 大変 (serious/difficult/terrible), not the adverbial 'very/terribly' sense. Mislabeled pos-sense pairing can mislead usage (adv 大変 only intensifies).
findings.suggested: serious; tough; terrible (move under adj-na sense, e.g. 大変だ; adv sense is only 'very/terribly')
findings.fix: serious; tough; terrible (move under adj-na sense, e.g. 大変だ; adv sense is only 'very/terribly')

findings.issue: Two glosses are joined inside a single array element ('student, pupil') instead of being separate gloss items, breaking the one-gloss-per-element format used everywhere else in the batch.
findings.suggested: student | pupil (as two separate array elements)
findings.fix: student | pupil (as two separate array elements)

findings.issue: 'gostado' is not natural Brazilian Portuguese as a standalone adjective gloss (bare past participle of 'gostar' is not used this way); the other glosses already cover the meaning.

"To sting, to bite (insect)" is the meaning of the homophone 刺す (sasu), not 差す. The entry 差す (JMdict 1291730-family senses) covers shining light, holding up an umbrella, inserting, pouring, etc. — never insect stings. This teaches another word's gloss.
findings.suggested: to shine (of sunlight), to stream in
findings.fix: to shine (of sunlight), to stream in

findings.issue: "Picar, ferroar" translates the sting/bite sense of the homophone 刺す, not any sense of 差す. Must be replaced together with the EN gloss (e.g. with the 'sunlight shining in' sense of 差す).

Glosses belong to the homophone 彼(かれ), not this lexeme 彼(あれ). JMdict 1000580 is the pronoun あれ = 'that; that thing (distant from both speaker and listener)'. Teaching あれ = 'he/him' is false, and the real core meaning is missing.
findings.suggested: that; that thing (distant from both speaker and listener)
findings.fix: that; that thing (distant from both speaker and listener)

findings.issue: 'ele' mistranslates あれ (it renders the homophone かれ). あれ is the distal demonstrative pronoun; pt should be 'aquilo/aquele'.
'boyfriend' is a sense of 彼(かれ), not of 彼(あれ). あれ's secondary person-referring sense is 'that person (referred to familiarly or dismissively)'.
'namorado' follows the wrong-lexeme EN gloss (かれ sense). Not a meaning of あれ.

接見(せっけん) is a formal/legal term (audience; lawyer's interview with a detainee), far beyond N5; likely a homophone mix-up with the actual N5 word 石鹸 (せっけん, 'soap'). Glosses match 接見 itself, so the defect is its inclusion at N5.
findings.suggested: remove from N5 (intended N5 lexeme is likely 石鹸 せっけん 'soap'); re-level 接見 much higher
findings.fix: remove from N5 (intended N5 lexeme is likely 石鹸 せっけん 'soap'); re-level 接見 much higher

findings.issue: あの is adnominal (adj-pn) and always precedes a noun, so the standalone pronoun 'aquilo' cannot render it (that is あれ). Keep only the adjectival forms aquele/aquela.
'gate' is not a sense of modern 戸(と) (gate is 門); 戸 means door, esp. a sliding/Japanese-style door or shutter. JMdict lists only 'door (esp. Japanese-style)'.
'portão' mirrors the incorrect EN 'gate'; 戸(と) is a porta (de correr), not a portão (門).

'em ponto' means 'sharp / on the dot' (exactness), which the hour suffix 〜時 does not convey — that nuance is ちょうど. A learner would wrongly think 3時 means '3 em ponto'. The EN gloss 'o'clock' just marks the hour ('...horas').

本島 'main island' is not an N5 vocabulary item on any community JLPT list; it was almost certainly swept into N5 via homophone confusion with 本当 (ほんとう), which is the real N5 word (and is present separately as vocab:1523060). Glosses themselves are correct for the lexeme.
findings.suggested: remove N5 tag / drop entry from the N5 set (homophone of 本当)
findings.fix: remove N5 tag / drop entry from the N5 set (homophone of 本当)

findings.issue: 'abafado' means muggy/stuffy (implies humidity and lack of air, i.e. 蒸し暑い), a nuance not present in 暑い 'hot' nor in the EN gloss set; it can mislead learners into using 暑い for 'stuffy'.
